notable_absence.finding: This page states 'Ephemeral buckets and their items exist only in memory and are never written to disk', which reads as a blanket no-tombstones claim for Ephemeral buckets - but memory.json's Ejection section (memory.md) states the opposite for a narrower case: ejecting an item from an Ephemeral bucket 'keeps a tombstone (a record of the ejected item, including keys and metadata) until the next scheduled metadata purge for the current node.' Both quotes are accurate to their own pages; the apparent tension is that this page's blanket disk-persistence statement doesn't carve out the in-memory tombstone case memory.md documents. Recorded as a cross-page tension rather than resolved, since resolving it would require reading past what either page states on its own.

cross_component_finding: storage-engines.md sends the reader here for Magma's flushing/compaction thread details ('See Magma Flushing and Compaction Threads for more information') and this page's Magma Flushing and Compaction Threads section is the only place those settings (num_storage_threads, magma_flusher_thread_percentage) are actually documented - confirming the split noted from the other side in storage-engines.json's cross_component_finding.
